note: Literature leads for the momentum family. Summaries are paraphrases from search-result abstracts (not verbatim quotes). These papers motivate the hypotheses; they are not evidence that the rules are profitable after costs on Binance perps.

papers.cite: Liu, Y. and Tsyvinski, A. (2021). Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency. Review of Financial Studies 34(6):2689-2727.
papers.paraphrase: Documents strong time-series momentum in BTC/ETH/XRP returns at 1-8 week horizons; investor-attention proxies forecast returns.
papers.relevance: Motivates TS momentum (config family a) at weekly horizon.

papers.cite: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A. and Wu, X. (2022). Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency. Journal of Finance 77(2). DOI 10.1111/jofi.13119.
papers.paraphrase: A three-factor model (market, size, momentum) prices the cross-section of coin returns; momentum factor built from past 1-4 week returns, weekly rebalanced, on spot coins (CoinMarketCap data, 2014-2018 era).
papers.relevance: Motivates cross-sectional momentum (family b) with weekly rebalancing and L of 1-4 weeks.

papers.cite: Moskowitz, T., Ooi, Y.H. and Pedersen, L.H. (2012). Time Series Momentum. Journal of Financial Economics 104(2):228-250.
papers.paraphrase: Past 12-month excess return predicts next-month return across 58 futures; positions volatility-scaled to a constant target.
papers.relevance: Source of the volatility-scaling construction used in family (a).

papers.cite: Grobys, K. and Sapkota, N. (2019). Cryptocurrencies and momentum. Economics Letters 180:6-10.
papers.paraphrase: 143 coins 2014-2018: no significant cross-sectional momentum payoffs.
papers.relevance: Contrary evidence; reason to expect XS momentum may fail.

papers.cite: Han, Kang and Ryu. Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market (working paper / AUT ACFR conference).
papers.paraphrase: TS momentum evidence strong, XS momentum weak; after transaction costs and intraday liquidations many significant gross returns become insignificant.
papers.relevance: Cost realism warning; motivates explicit fees, slippage and funding.
